title: In vivo regeneration of neo-nephrons in rodents by renal progenitor cell transplantation
protocol: Mate female/male B6;129-Six2[tm3(EGFP/cre/ERT2) Amc]/J (Six2-GCE) mice with male/female B6;129-Gt(ROSA)26Sor[tm1(DTA) Mrc]/J (Rosa26-DTA176) mice.
Use timed mating, considering 12 pm of the day that the vaginal plug was detected as 0.5 days post-coitum.
Identify offspring Six2-DTA mice based on the expression of Six2-green fluorescent protein (GFP) by neural progenitor cells (NPCs) in motor neurons (MNs) under a fluorescent stereomicroscope.
Note: Motor neurons contain renal progenitor cells, which include NPCs, stromal progenitor cells, and ureteric buds.
Culture MNs of Six2-DTA mice on embryonic day 13.5 (E13.5) with 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4OHT).
Perform immunostaining to reveal atrophy of the MNs and almost complete elimination of Six2-expressing NPCs in Six2-DTA mice.
Culture metanephroses isolated from GFP-labeled mice and rats enzymatically.
Prepare the dissociated RPCs from the MNs of GFP-labeled mice or rats for subsequent injections into the nephrogenic zone.
Euthanize the GFP-mouse at 13.5–14.5 days of pregnancy by dislocation of the cervical vertebrae.
Remove the uteruses through a median incision and place them in a 10-cm dish containing Hanks' Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) with calcium and magnesium but without phenol red.
Extract the embryos from the isolated uteruses and euthanize them by decapitation.
Collect pairs of MNs from embryos using micro-tweezers under a stereoscopic microscope.
Remove the tail from the decapitated embryo.
Dissect both sides along the vertebral column from the caudal end to the neck.
Cut both sides of the rib cage.
Remove the vertebral column from the body.
Place the embryo in a prone position.
Collect MNs into a 1.5-mL tube with 1 mL of minimum essential medium α (MEM α).
Dissociate MNs using a modified Davies et al. protocol.
Centrifuge MNs at 700 × g for 3 min.
Remove supernatants and add 1 mL of Accutase to the tube.
Vortex to aid digestion.
Incubate MNs at 37°C for 15 min, vortex after 5 min.
Manually pipette using a 200-μL pipette tip after 10 and 15 min.
Centrifuge MNs at 300 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatants and resuspend the pellet with 1 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Dissociate MNs by manual pipetting with a 200-μL pipette tip.
Filter the cell suspension using a 40-μm cell strainer to obtain a single-cell suspension.
Centrifuge the suspension at 700 × g for 3 min.
Completely remove the supernatants.
Tap and mix the pellet.
Pause Point: The pellet can be incubated on ice until its use within the same day, though incubation for more than 4 h leads to a decline in cell viability.
Anesthetize pregnant rats by isoflurane inhalation when extracting embryos from GFP-rats.
Euthanize the mother immediately by pentobarbital (120 mg/kg) infusion after removing the uteruses.
Stain the sample with Trypan Blue before centrifugation, if optional step 5f is performed.
Observe under a light microscope to determine the cell number and viability.
Maintain 201B7 cells on iMatrix-511 in StemFit AK02N.
Culture the cells in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2 at 37°C in 6-well plates.
Passage the cells every 6 days when they reach 70%-80% confluence.
Treat confluent cells with Accutase before passage.
Seed cells into another well with a diameter of 35 mm at a concentration of 1.5 × 10^4 cells per well.
Reaggregate hiPSCs at 10,000 cells/aggregate in V-bottom 96-well low cell-binding plates.
Add base media for human NPCs supplemented with 10 μM Y27632, 1 ng/mL human Activin A, and 20 ng/mL human basic fibroblast growth factor (FGF-basic).
Transfer the spheres to U-bottom 96-well low-cell-binding plates containing base media for human NPCs supplemented with 10 μM CHIR and 10 μM Y27632 after 24 hours.
Replace half of the culture media with new media every other day starting from days 3 and 5.

On day 7, transfer the spheres to new U-bottom plates containing the base media for human NPCs supplemented with 10 ng/mL human Activin A, 3 ng/mL human bone morphogenetic protein 4 (Bmp4), 3 μM CHIR, 0.1 μM retinoic acid, and 10 μM Y27632 (200 μL/well).
On day 9, transfer the spheres to new U-bottom plates containing the base media for human NPCs supplemented with 1 μM CHIR, 5 ng/mL fibroblast growth factor-9 (FGF-9), and 10 μM Y27632 (200 μL/well).
On day 12, incubate NPCs in 5 mL of Enzyme Solution at 37°C for 30 min.
Centrifuge the NPCs at 190 × g for 4 min to pellet them.
Resuspend the pellets in 5 mL of Dispersion solution.
Add 5 mL of Isolation solution.
Pellet the NPCs by centrifugation at 160 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the pellets in 1 mL of PBS and filter through a 40-μm cell strainer.
Centrifuge again at 160 × g for 5 min to pellet them completely.
Remove the supernatant entirely.
Tap the tube to mix the pellet thoroughly.
Incubate on ice until use within the same day.
Perform flow cytometry to confirm the purity of NPCs in NPSs before injections into the nephrogenic zone.
Characterize NPCs by the presence of integrin α8 (ITGA8) and absence of platelet-derived growth factor receptor α (PDGFRα).
Use about 5 × 10^5 cells from single-cell solution for cell staining.
Treat the solution with biotinylated anti-ITGA8, APC-conjugated streptavidin, and PE-conjugated anti-PDGFRα.
Acquire and analyze data using MACSQuantify analysis software.
Inject RPCs (dissociated from MNs of GFP-mice and GFP-rats) and human NPCs into the nephrogenic zone under the MN capsule of Six2-DTA mice.
Culture MNs that underwent injections in vitro and in vivo.
Inject exogenous RPCs into the nephrogenic zone.
Use RPCs from GFP-mice or GFP-rats, or NPCs from hiPSCs in each experiment.
Fix the embryo with micro-tweezers.
Fill the glass needle with the dissociated exogenous RPCs.
Insert the glass needle through the renal hilus to the nephrogenic zone under the capsule.
Inject cells slowly by mouth pipetting under a stereoscopic microscope (M205FA, Leica Microsystems).
Use a 1-mL syringe and an aspirator tube assembly connected to the glass needle.
Inject 4–8 × 104 cells into the nephrogenic zone using a glass needle.
Pull out the needle carefully to avoid rupturing the capsule.
Inject exogenous RPCs into the subcapsular area, not the renal parenchyma.
Perform several injections (up to 2–4) to cover the required area.
Advance the glass needle immediately before the capsule to spread RPCs in the nephrogenic zone.
Remove supernatants entirely from centrifuged pellets to avoid tearing the capsule with large droplets.
Detach the MNs from the embryos of Six2-DTA mice containing exogenous RPCs.
Place the isolated MNs on the air-fluid interface of polycarbonate filters with an average pore size of 0.4 μm (12-mm Transwell plates).
Soak the plates with base media for MNs supplemented with 4OHT.
Culture MNs for 7 days at 37°C in a 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Change the media and add 4OHT daily.
Transplant MNs with the ureters and bladder into the retroperitoneum of adult NOD/Shi-scid, IL-2RγKO Jic mice or LEW/SsNSlc rats with tamoxifen.
Detach the MNBs from the embryos of Six2-DTA mice.
Remove the bilateral mesonephroses and the intestine connected to the MNs carefully.
Dissect both groins vertically to reveal the bladder.
Insert micro-tweezers under the metanephroses to peel off the connective tissue.
Cut the cranial side of the MNs.
Lift the MNs and remove the remaining intestine and spleen.
Cut the root of the bladder to detach the MNBs.
Trim the MNBs.
Incubate MNBs in HBSS on ice for less than 4 hours.
Anesthetize host animals by isoflurane inhalation.
Reveal the descending aorta via a median incision.
Cut the retroperitoneum horizontally, approximately 1-2 mm around the descending aorta.
Make a pocket using micro-tweezers under a surgical microscope.
Transplant isolated MNBs into the pocket.
Dissolve tamoxifen in corn oil at a concentration of 40 mg/mL.
Treat host animals with tamoxifen by daily oral gavage for six days, starting one day before transplantation (NOG mice: 200 mg/kg/day; Lewis rats: 60 mg/kg/day).
Administer 2 mg/kg tacrolimus subcutaneously and 5 mg/kg methylprednisolone intraperitoneally daily to Lewis rats starting the day before transplantation.
Administer intravenous tetramethylrhodamine-labeled dextran (10,000 MW, 200 μL of 5 mg/mL) daily to a few NOG mice starting five days prior to MNB collection.
Euthanize host animals by intraperitoneal pentobarbital infusion two or four weeks later.
Remove transplanted MNBs for histological analysis.
Fix the MNs on Transwell plates with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Wash the samples with 0.1% TWEEN 20/PBS three times at 15°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Block the samples using PBS with 1% donkey serum, 0.2% skimmed milk, and 0.3% Triton X at 15°C–25°C for 1 hour.
Wash the samples with 0.1% TWEEN 20/PBS three times at 15°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Incubate the samples at 4°C for 12–18 hours with primary antibodies diluted in PBS with 1% donkey serum, 0.2% skimmed milk, and 0.3% Triton X (1:100).
Wash the samples with 0.1% TWEEN 20/PBS three times at 15°C–25°C for 1 hour.

Incubate the samples with secondary antibodies conjugated with Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 546, or Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200), together with 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI, 1:2,000), diluted in PBS with 1% donkey serum, 0.2% skimmed milk, and 0.3% Triton X, at 15°C–25°C for 1 hour.
Wash the samples with 0.1% TWEEN 20/PBS three times at 15°C–25°C for 30 minutes.
Mount the samples using SlowFade Diamond Antifade Mountant.
Examine the samples under a confocal laser scanning microscope (LSM880, Zeiss).
Create frozen sections of neo-nephrons regenerated in vivo.
Analyze their differentiation morphologically by Hematoxylin-eosin staining and immunostaining.
Fix the MNs in 4% paraformaldehyde for 3 h.
Dehydrate the fixed MNs with 20% sucrose in PBS at 4°C for 12–18 h.
Embed the MNs with optimal cutting temperature (OCT) compound.
Cryosection the embedded MNs to obtain 8-μm-thick sections.
Perform Hematoxylin-eosin staining according to standard protocols for histological analysis.
Examine the samples under a microscope (BZ-X800, KEYENCE).
Wash the sections with PBS three times at 15°C–25°C for 5 min.
Incubate the sections in 10% HistoVT One/PBS at 70°C for 20 min.
Wash the sections with 0.1% TWEEN 20/PBS twice at 15°C–25°C for 5 min.
For blocking, add the Blocking One Histo buffer directly to the sections and incubate them at 15°C–25°C for 10 min.
Wash the sections once with 0.1% TWEEN 20/PBS at 15°C–25°C for 5 min.
Incubate the sections with primary antibodies diluted in Signal Enhancer HIKARI for Immunostain Solution A (1:100) at 4°C for 12–18 h.
Wash the sections with 0.1% TWEEN 20/PBS three times at 15°C–25°C for 5 min.
Incubate the sections with secondary antibodies diluted in Signal Enhancer HIKARI for Immunostain Solution A (1:200) at 15°C–25°C for 1 h.
Wash the sections once with 0.1% TWEEN 20/PBS at 15°C–25°C for 5 min.
Mount the sections with Prolong Gold Antifade Mountant with DAPI.
Examine the samples under a confocal laser scanning microscope (LSM880, Zeiss) or a fluorescence microscope (BZ-X800, KEYENCE).
Perform RT-qPCR to analyze the expression of nephron markers in regenerated nephrons and compare it with that of RPCs and native MNs.
Isolate total RNA from collected samples using the RNeasy Micro Kit according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Treat isolated RNA with gDNA Eraser as per the PrimeScript RT Reagent Kit instructions.
Synthesize cDNA using 50 ng of RNA template for each sample.
Conduct a RT-qPCR analysis of the cDNAs using TaqMan Master Mix and TaqMan assay on a thermocycler (Rotor-Gene Q, Qiagen).
Normalize expression levels of target markers with those of the glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase (Gaphd) gene.
